verses.zh: 但愿我的头为水，我的眼为泪的泉源，我好为我百姓（原文是民女；七节同）中被杀的人昼夜哭泣。
verses.en: (8:23)[NOTE:1] I wish that my head were a well full of water[NOTE:2] and my eyes were a fountain full of tears!If they were, I could cry day and night for those of my dear people[NOTE:3] who have been killed.
notes: Beginning with 9:1, the verse numbers through 9:26 in the English Bible differ from the verse numbers in the Hebrew text (BHS), with 9:1 ET = 8:23 HT, 9:2 ET = 9:1 HT, 9:3 ET = 9:2 HT, etc., through 9:26 ET = 9:25 HT. Beginning with 10:1 the verse numbers in the ET and HT are again the same.
Heb “I wish that my head were water.”
Heb “daughter of my people.” For the translation given here see 4:11 and the note on the phrase “dear people” there.
verses.commentary:
9:1 The prophet is using emotional figurative language to express his pain over YHWH's necessary
judgment of His covenant people (cf. Heb. 12:5-11). In reality it is YHWH's pain that the prophet is
revealing (cf. Hosea 11:8-9). This same emotion is seen in Jer. 8:18; 13:17; Isa. 22:4; Lam. 2:18.

This verse is one of the sources of Jeremiah being known as "the weeping prophet." He was
such because YHWH was weeping through him (cf. Hosea 11:8-9).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (ANTHROPOMORPHISM)

▣ "the daughter of my people" See full note at Jer. 46:11.

verses.zh: 惟愿我在旷野有行路人住宿之处，使我可以离开我的民出去；因他们都是行奸淫的，是行诡诈的一党。
verses.en: (9:1) I wish I had a lodging place in the wildernesswhere I could spend some time like a weary traveler.[NOTE:1] Then I would desert my peopleand walk away from thembecause they are all unfaithful to God,a congregation[NOTE:2] of people that has been disloyal to him.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “I wish I had in the desert a lodging place [inn, or place to spend the night] for travelers.”
Or “bunch,” but this loses the irony; the word is used for the solemn assemblies at the religious feasts.
Heb “they are all adulterers, a congregation of unfaithful people.” However, spiritual adultery is, of course, meant, not literal adultery. So the literal translation would be misleading.
verses.commentary:
9:2-4 Notice how the prophet/YHWH describes the covenant people.

- adulteress, Jer. 9:2

- treacherous men, Jer. 9:2

- lie, Jer. 9:3

- evil to evil, Jer. 9:3

- do not know YHWH, Jer. 9:3

- untrustworthy, Jer. 9:4

- crafty, Jer. 9:4

- slanderer, Jer. 9:4

- deceiver, Jer. 9:5

- do not speak truth, Jer. 9:5

- liars, Jer. 9:5

- commit iniquity, Jer. 9:5

- deceitful, Jer. 9:6

- refuse to know YHWH, Jer. 9:6

And these are the people of God. He must do something lest His purpose for this planet
is lost (cf. Ezek. 36:22-36).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

9:2 "A wayfarers' lodging place" This was a lean-to or an uninhabited wooden shelter used by
travelers in desert areas. What shocking imagery that God's prophet wanted to run away from
(i.e. two Qal COHORTATIVES, "leave" and "go") the covenant people and hide in
the desert. The pain of YHWH's judgment overwhelmed him! YHWH's people surely deserved it, but the
curses of Lev. 26 and Deut. 28 were so violent and painful.

▣ "For all of them are adulterers

An assembly of treacherous men" There is an obvious comparison and play on
these two phrases as a title for the people of God. Their lifestyle and attitude reflected both
physical and spiritual adultery (i.e. idolatry in general or fertility worship).

verses.zh: 他们弯起舌头像弓一样，为要说谎话。他们在国中增长势力，不是为行诚实，乃是恶上加恶，并不认识我。这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: The Lord says,[NOTE:1] “These people are like soldiers who have readied their bows.Their tongues are always ready to shoot out lies.[NOTE:2] They have become powerful in the land, but they have not done so by honest means.[NOTE:3] Indeed, they do one evil thing after another[NOTE:4] and do not pay attention to me.[NOTE:5]
notes: The words “The Lord says” have been moved up from the end of the verse to make clear that a change in speaker has occurred.
Heb “They have readied [or strung] their tongue as their bow for lies.”
Heb “but not through honesty.”
Heb “they go from evil to evil.”

Or “do not acknowledge me”; Heb “do not know me.” But “knowing” in Hebrew thought often involves more than intellectual knowledge; it involves emotional and volitional commitment as well. For יָדַע (yadaʿ) meaning “acknowledge” see 1 Chr 28:9; Isa 29:21; Hos 2:20; Prov 3:6. This word is also found in ancient Near Eastern treaty contexts where it has the idea of a vassal king acknowledging the sovereignty of a greater king (cf. H. Huffmon, “The Treaty Background of Hebrew yada,” BASOR 181 [1966]: 31-37).
verses.commentary:
9:3 "They bend their tongue like their bow" Their speech showed who and what they really
were (cf. Jer. 9:8). This imagery seems to refer to one of three things.

- their tongues were bent which reflected the words for sin, a deviation from the standard

- they were ready to shoot their words at anyone (cf. Ps. 64:3-4)

- it refers to the pain that their lies caused both to God and their fellow Israelites
(cf. Lev. 19:15-16)

SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN SPEECH

▣ "And they do not know Me" This is the tragedy—the pain that God felt
(cf. Jer. 2:13; 17:13; Hosea 4:1,6; 5:4; 8:2; 11:8-9) after He had given so much to this people and they had knowingly,
willfully turned their backs on Him. There is a word to the church today in these verses.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

verses.zh: 你们各人当谨防邻舍，不可信靠弟兄；因为弟兄尽行欺骗，邻舍都往来谗谤人。
verses.en: Everyone must be on his guard around his friends.He must not even trust any of his relatives.[NOTE:1] For every one of them will find some way to cheat him.[NOTE:2] And all his friends will tell lies about him.
notes: Heb “Be on your guard…Do not trust.” The verbs are second masculine plural of direct address and there seems no way to translate literally and not give the mistaken impression that Jeremiah is being addressed. This is another example of the tendency in Hebrew style to turn from description to direct address (a figure of speech called apostrophe).

There is perhaps an intentional pun and allusion here to Gen 27:36 and the wordplay on the name Jacob there. The text here reads עָקוֹב יַעְקֹב (ʿaqob yaʿqob).tn Heb “cheating, each of them will cheat.”
verses.commentary:
9:4 Even among the covenant people, there is no "trust" (BDB 105). They not only lie, cheat, and steal from
others, but from each other. The terrible results of the Fall are obvious.

- let everyone be on guard against his neighbor ‒ BDB 1036, KB 1581, Niphal
IMPERATIVE

- do not trust any brother ‒ BDB 105, KB 120, Qal IMPERFECT used in a
JUSSIVE sense

- craftily ‒ this is an INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and an
IMPERFECT VERB from the same root (BDB 784, KB 872), which shows intensity

The people of God were more like Jacob (supplanter, BDB 784) than Israel.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

verses.zh: 他们各人欺哄邻舍，不说真话；他们教舌头学习说谎，劳劳碌碌地作孽。
verses.en: One friend deceives another,and no one tells the truth.These people have trained themselves[NOTE:1] to tell lies.They do wrong and are unable to repent.
notes: Heb “their tongues.” However, this is probably not a natural idiom in contemporary English, and the tongue may stand as a part for the whole anyway.
verses.commentary:
9:5 "They weary themselves committing iniquity" What a horrible description of God's people as
they go headlong into rebellion and idolatry (BDB 521, KB 512, Niphal PERFECT).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SIN IN THE OT, A. #2

verses.zh: 你的住处在诡诈的人中；他们因行诡诈，不肯认识我。这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: They do one act of violence after another,and one deceitful thing after another.[NOTE:1] They refuse to pay attention to me,”[NOTE:2] says the Lord.
notes: An alternate reading for vv. 5d-6b is, “They wear themselves out doing wrong. Jeremiah, you live in the midst of deceitful people. They deceitfully refuse to take any thought of/acknowledge me.” The translation which has been adopted is based on a redivision of the lines, a redivision of some of the words, and a revocalization of some of the consonants. The MT reads literally, “doing wrong they weary themselves. Your sitting in the midst of deceit; in deceit they refuse to know me” (הַעֲוֵה נִלְאוּ׃ שִׁבְתְּךָ בְּתוֹךְ מִרְמָה בְּמִרְמָה מֵאֲנוּ דַעַת־אוֹתִי). The Greek version reads literally, “they do wrong and they do not cease to turn themselves around. Usury upon usury and deceit upon deceit. They do not want to know me.” This suggests that one should read the Hebrew text as הַעֲוֵה נִלְאוּ שֻׁב׃ תֹּךְ בְּתוֹךְ מִרְמָה בְּמִרְמָה מֵאֲנוּ דַעַת אוֹתִי, which translated literally yields, “doing evil [= “they do evil,” using the Hiphil infinitive absolute as a finite verb (cf. GKC 346 §113.ff)], they are not able [cf. KBL 468 s.v. לָאָה Niph.3 and see Exod 7:18 for parallel use] to repent. Oppression on oppression [cf. BDB 1067 s.v. תֹּךְ, II תּוֹךְ]; deceit on deceit. They refuse to know me.” This reading has ancient support and avoids the introduction of an unexpected second masculine suffix into the context. It has been adopted here, along with a number of modern commentaries (cf., e.g., W. McKane, Jeremiah [ICC], 1:201) and English versions, as the more likely reading.
Or “do not acknowledge me”; Heb “do not know me.” See the note on the phrase “do not take any thought of me” in 9:3.
verses.commentary:
9:6 "Your dwelling is in the midst of deceit" This describes the covenant people's worldview
and daily lifestyle!

▣ "they refuse to know Me" The VERB (BDB 549, KB 540, Piel
PERFECT) denotes a settled condition. They are not duped but willful rejecters of truth.

For "know" see SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

verses.zh: 所以万军之耶和华如此说：看哪，我要将他们熔化熬炼；不然，我因我百姓的罪该怎样行呢？
verses.en: Therefore the Lord of Heaven’s Armies says:[NOTE:1] “I will now purify them in the fires of affliction[NOTE:2] and test them.The wickedness of my dear people[NOTE:3] has left me no choice.What else can I do?[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “Yahweh of armies.”sn For the significance of this title see the notes at 2:19 and 7:3.
Heb “I will refine/purify them.” The words “in the fires of affliction” are supplied in the translation to give clarity to the metaphor.
Heb “daughter of my people.” For the translation given here see 4:11 and the note on the phrase “dear people” there.

Heb “For how else shall I deal because of the wickedness of the daughter of my people.” The MT does not have the word “wickedness.” The word, however, is read in the Greek version. This is probably a case of a word dropping out because of its similarities to the consonants preceding or following it (i.e., haplography). The word “wickedness” (רַעַת, raʿat) has dropped out before the words “my dear people” (בַּת־עַמִּי, bat-ʿammi). The causal nuance which is normal for מִפְּנֵי (mippene) does not make sense without some word like this, and the combination of מִפְּנֵי רַעַת (mippene raʿat) does occur in Jer 7:12 and one very like it occurs in Jer 26:3.
verses.commentary:
9:7-9 This is another strophe listing Judah's sins.

- liars

- ambush neighbors

YHWH must act!

- He will refine and assay them (cf. Jer. 6:27)

- He will punish them (cf. Jer. 5:9,29)

- He will avenge Himself (cf. Isa. 1:24)

YHWH wants to use the covenant people to reach all other nations. He has an eternal
redemptive plan. However, His people have not revealed Him, but rather their own weaknesses and
failures. Therefore, YHWH Himself must act (cf. Ezek. 36:22-36).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

verses.zh: 他们的舌头是毒箭，说话诡诈；人与邻舍口说和平话，心却谋害他。
verses.en: Their tongues are like deadly arrows.[NOTE:1] They are always telling lies.[NOTE:2] Friendly words for their neighbors come from their mouths,but their minds are thinking up ways to trap them.[NOTE:3]
notes: This reading follows the Masoretic consonants (the Kethib, a Qal active participle from שָׁחַט, shakhat). The Masoretes preferred to read “a sharpened arrow” (the Qere, a Qal passive participle from the same root or a homonym, meaning “hammered, beaten”). See HALOT 1354 s.v. II שָׁחַט for discussion. The exact meaning of the word makes little difference to the meaning of the metaphor itself.
Heb “They speak deceit.”
Heb “With his mouth a person speaks peace to his neighbor, but in his heart he sets an ambush for him.”

verses.zh: 耶和华说：我岂不因这些事讨他们的罪呢？岂不报复这样的国民呢？
verses.en: I will certainly punish them for doing such things!” says the Lord.“I will certainly bring retribution on such a nation as this!”[NOTE:1]
notes: See 5:9, 29. This is somewhat of a refrain at the end of a catalog of Judah’s sins.tn Heb “Should I not punish them…? Should I not bring retribution…?” The rhetorical questions function as emphatic declarations.
verses.commentary:
9:9 "On a nation such as this" This is a play on the word goy (BDB 156), which the Jews
used in derision for the Gentiles. Here it is used to describe Israel herself.

▣ "Shall I not avenge Myself?" All sin and disobedience of the covenant people was not only
against His word but Himself (cf. Jer. 5:9,29).

verses.zh: 我要为山岭哭泣悲哀，为旷野的草场扬声哀号；因为都已干焦，甚至无人经过。人也听不见牲畜鸣叫，空中的飞鸟和地上的野兽都已逃去。
verses.en: I said,[NOTE:1] “I will weep and mourn[NOTE:2] for the grasslands on the mountains;[NOTE:3] I will sing a mournful song for the pastures in the wildernessbecause they are so scorched no one travels through them.The sound of livestock is no longer heard there.Even the birds in the sky and the wild animals in the fieldshave fled and are gone.”
notes: The words “I said” are not in the text, but there is general agreement that Jeremiah is the speaker. Cf. the lament in 8:18-9:1. These words are supplied in the translation for clarity. Some English versions follow the Greek text which reads a plural imperative here. Since this reading would make the transition between 9:10 and 9:11 easier, it is probably not original but a translator’s way of smoothing over a difficulty.
Heb “I will lift up weeping and mourning.”

Heb “for the mountains.” However, the context makes clear that it is the grasslands or pastures on the mountains that are meant. The words “for the grasslands” are supplied in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
9:10-11 Again the question arises as to who is speaking in these two verses. The NIV translates
Jer. 9:10 as the prophet speaking and Jer. 9:11 as God speaking. But the NASV and RSV translate them as
God speaking in both verses. It is basically extended imagery that the land is being affected by
the covenant peoples' continuous sin, and there are consequences (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28; Rom. 8:18-22).

verses.zh: 我必使耶路撒冷变为乱堆，为野狗的住处，也必使犹大的城邑变为荒场，无人居住。
verses.en: The Lord said,[NOTE:1] “I will make Jerusalem[NOTE:2] a heap of ruins.Jackals will make their home there.[NOTE:3] I will destroy the towns of Judahso that no one will be able to live in them.”
notes: The words “the Lord said” are not in the text, but it is obvious from the content that he is the speaker. These words are supplied in the translation for clarity.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “a heap of ruins, a haunt for jackals.”

verses.zh: 谁是智慧人，可以明白这事？耶和华的口向谁说过，使他可以传说？遍地为何灭亡，干焦好像旷野，甚至无人经过呢？
verses.en: I said,[NOTE:1] “Who is wise enough to understand why this has happened?[NOTE:2] Who has a word from the Lord that can explain it?[NOTE:3] Why does the land lie in ruins?Why is it as scorched as a desert through which no one travels?”
notes: The words, “I said” are not in the text. It is not clear that a shift in speaker has taken place. However, the words of the verse are very unlikely to be a continuation of the Lord’s threat. It is generally assumed that these are the words of Jeremiah and that a dialogue is going on between him and the Lord in vv. 9-14. That assumption is accepted here.
Heb “Who is the wise man that he may understand this?”
Heb “And [who is the man] to whom the mouth of the Lord has spoken, that he may explain it?”
verses.commentary:
9:12-16 These verses are a strong statement by God (introduced by three questions in Jer. 9:12)
on the results of Judah's rebellion. In Jer. 9:13 and 14 the reasons for the exile are enumerated.

- they have forsaken My law (written revelation, cf. Exodus 19-20; Deut. 4:8; 5)

- they have not obeyed My voice (oral prophetic revelation)

- they have not walked according to My voice

- they walked after the stubbornness of their heart (cf. Jer. 7:24; 11:8)

- they walked after the Ba'als (cf. Jer. 2:8,23; 23:27)

Revelation should result in godly lifestyle (cf. Hosea 14:9)!

verses.zh: 耶和华说：「因为这百姓离弃我，在他们面前所设立的律法没有遵行，也没有听从我的话；
verses.en: The Lord answered, “This has happened because these people have rejected my laws that I gave them. They have not obeyed me or followed those laws.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and they have not walked in it [with “it” referring to “my law”].”

verses.zh: 只随从自己顽梗的心行事，照他们列祖所教训的随从众巴力。」
verses.en: Instead they have followed the stubborn inclinations of their own hearts. They have paid allegiance to[NOTE:1] the gods called Baal,[NOTE:2] as their fathers[NOTE:3] taught them to do.
notes: Heb “they have gone/followed after.” See the translator’s note at 2:5 for the idiom.
Heb “the Baals,” referring either to the pagan gods called “Baals” or the images of Baal (so NLT).
Or “forefathers,” or “ancestors.” Here the referent could be the immediate parents or, by their example, more distant ancestors.
verses.commentary:
9:14 "walked after the stubbornness of their heart" This is a characteristic of the Jewish people
delineated in the book of Deuteronomy. God's mercy is seen against the backdrop of their natural tendency to
rebellion (cf. Deut. 9:6,13; 10:16; 31:27). It also says that they walked away open-eyed; they were not
tricked nor did they do it in ignorance!

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS (OT)

▣ "and after the Baals" This refers to the fertility worship of Canaan. Originally El
and Ashtorah were the chief deities of the Canaanite pantheon (Ras Shamra texts from Ugarit).
Ba'al was their son. The myth involved the rising and dying of the agricultural deity every year. By
the means of imitation magic, including the sex act, fertility was assured each spring. There was a
Ba'al shrine for every city and village.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE

▣ "as their fathers taught them" This may be an historical allusion to Exodus 32 and
Numbers 25. This shows the potential corruption from one generation to the next (cf. Deut. 5:9;
Isa. 29:13). Family faith can be a blessing or a curse depending on the content (cf. Jer. 7:18)!

verses.zh: 所以万军之耶和华―以色列的　神如此说：「看哪，我必将茵蔯给这百姓吃，又将苦胆水给他们喝。
verses.en: So then, listen to what I, the Lord of Heaven’s Armies, the God of Israel,[NOTE:1] say,[NOTE:2] ‘I will make these people eat the bitter food of suffering and drink the poison water of judgment.[NOTE:3]
notes: See the study notes on 2:9 and 7:3.tn Heb “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel.”
Heb “Therefore, thus says the Lord…” The person is shifted from third to first to better conform with English style.

Heb “I will feed this people wormwood and make them drink poison water.” “Wormwood” and “poison water” are not to be understood literally here but are symbolic of judgment and suffering. See, e.g., BDB 542 s.v. לַעֲנָה.
verses.commentary:
9:15 "wormwood. . .poisoned water" The false family faith of Jer. 9:14b reflects the curse
of Deut. 29:18. This was specifically mentioned in Jer. 8:14e. Notice it is YHWH, Himself, who gives
it! Sin has consequences, especially for those who know better (cf. Luke 12:48; Rom. 9:4-5).

verses.zh: 我要把他们散在列邦中，就是他们和他们列祖素不认识的列邦。我也要使刀剑追杀他们，直到将他们灭尽。」
verses.en: I will scatter them among nations that neither they nor their ancestors[NOTE:1] have known anything about. I will send people chasing after them with swords[NOTE:2] until I have destroyed them.’”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “fathers.”
Heb “I will send the sword after them.” The sword here is probably not completely literal but refers to death by violent means, including death by the sword.
He will destroy them but not completely. See Jer 5:18; 30:11; 46:28.
verses.commentary:
9:16 "I will scatter them among the nations" This is either an allusion to the exile of the
northern tribes in 722 B.C. by Assyria or it is a prophecy of the exile of the southern
tribes by Neo-Babylon in 605, 597, 586 or 582 B.C. Exile was one of the consequences of covenant
disobedience in Lev. 26:33; Deut. 28:64.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

verses.zh: 万军之耶和华如此说：你们应当思想，将善唱哀歌的妇女召来，又打发人召善哭的妇女来，
verses.en: The Lord of Heaven’s Armies[NOTE:1] told me to say to this people:[NOTE:2] “Take note of what I say.[NOTE:3] Call for the women who mourn for the dead!Summon those who are the most skilled at it!”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “Yahweh of Armies.”sn For the significance of this title see the notes at 2:19 and 7:3.

Heb “Thus says Yahweh of Armies.” However, without some addition it is not clear to whom the command is addressed. The words are supplied in the translation for clarity and to help resolve a rather confusing issue of who is speaking throughout vv. 16-21. As has been evident throughout the translation, the speaker is not always indicated. Sometimes it is not even clear who the speaker is. In general the translation and the notes have reflected the general consensus in identifying who it is. Here, however, there is a good deal of confusion about who is speaking in vv. 18, 20-21. The Greek translation has the Lord speaking throughout with second plural pronouns in vv. 18, 21 and the absence of the first line in v. 22. It would be hard to explain how the MT arose if the Greek reflected the original text. Critical commentators such as J. Bright, W. Holladay, and W. McKane resolve the issue by dropping out the introductory formula in v. 17 and the first line of v. 22 and assigning the whole lament to Jeremiah. It seems obvious from the first plural pronouns and the content of v. 18 (and probably v. 21 as well), and from the fact that the Lord is referred to in other than the first person in v. 20, that he is not the speaker of those verses. The translation attempts to resolve the issue by having Jeremiah report the Lord’s command in v. 17 and letting the rest of the speech be essentially that of Jeremiah. It should be admitted, however, that the issue is far from resolved. Most English versions simply ignore the problem. The GNB (= TEV) is a rare exception.
Heb “Consider!”
Heb “Call for the mourning women that they may come and send for the wise/skilled women that they may come.” The verbs here are masculine plural, addressed to the people.
verses.commentary:
9:17-22 This is a funeral dirge (cf. Jer. 9:20), personifying death. Notice the two terms for
professional mourners.

- "the mourning women" ‒ BDB 884, KB 1096, Polel PARTICIPLE

- "the wailing women" ‒ BDB 314, KB 314 (ADJECTIVE, lit. "unskilled")

Notice the number of commands.

- Verse 17

- "consider" ‒ BDB 106, KB 122, Hithpolel IMPERATIVE

- "call" ‒ BDB 894, KB 1128, Qal IMPERATIVE

- "come" ‒ BDB 97, KB 112, Qal IMPERFECT used in a
JUSSIVE sense

- "send" ‒ BDB 1018, KB 1511, Qal IMPERATIVE

- "come" ‒ same as c

- Verse 18

- "let them make haste" ‒ BDB 554, KB 553, Piel IMPERFECT used in a
JUSSIVE sense

- "let them take up a wailing for us" ‒ BDB 669, KB 724, Qal
IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

- "let our eyes shed tears" ‒ BDB 432, KB 434, Qal IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense (NRSV)

- "let our eyelids flow with water" ‒ BDB 633, KB 683, Qal IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense (NRSV)

- Verse 20

- "hear the word of the Lord" ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal
IMPERATIVE

- "let your ear receive the word of His mouth" ‒ BDB 542, KB 534, Qal
IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

- "teach. . ." ‒ BDB 540, KB 531, Piel IMPERATIVE

- Verse 22 ‒ "speak" ‒ BDB 180, KB 210, Piel IMPERATIVE

9:17 "the wailing women" In the Ancient Near East (ANE) professional mourners were used at
funerals (cf. Amos 5:16). Here it is a literary way to highlight the fact that death is coming.

In Jer. 9:20 the daughters are going to be taught how to wail. This is either an allusion
to the fact

- that the mothers passed on their idolatry to their daughters

- that there will be so many dead people that more and more wailers will be needed

verses.zh: 叫她们速速为我们举哀，使我们眼泪汪汪，使我们的眼皮涌出水来。
verses.en: I said, “Indeed,[NOTE:1] let them come quickly and sing a song of mourning for us.Let them wail loudly until tears stream from our own eyesand our eyelids overflow with water.
notes: The words “And I said, ‘Indeed’” are not in the text. They have been supplied in the translation to try and help clarify who the speaker is who identifies with the lament of the people.

verses.zh: 因为听见哀声出于锡安，说：我们怎样败落了！我们大大地惭愧！我们撇下地土；人也拆毁了我们的房屋。
verses.en: For the sound of wailing is soon to be heard in Zion,‘We are utterly ruined![NOTE:1] We are completely disgraced!For we have left our land,for our houses have been torn down!’”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “How we are ruined!”

Or “For we have left…because they have thrown down….” These probably offer parallel reasons for the cries, “We are utterly ruined…disgraced!” since the reason for leaving is not simply the destruction of their houses.
verses.commentary:
9:19 This verse expresses the content of their lamentations.

- we are ruined (cf. Jer. 4:13; Deut. 28:29)

- we are put to great shame

- we have left the land (cf. Jer. 7:15)

- our homes are destroyed

verses.zh: 妇女们哪，你们当听耶和华的话，领受他口中的言语；又当教导你们的儿女举哀，各人教导邻舍唱哀歌。
verses.en: I said,[NOTE:1] “So now,[NOTE:2] you wailing women, listen to the Lord’s message.[NOTE:3] Open your ears to the message from his mouth.Teach your daughters this mournful song,and let every woman teach her neighbor this lament.
notes: The words “I said” are not in the text. The text merely has, “Indeed, yes.” The words are supplied in the translation to indicate that the speaker is still Jeremiah, though he now is not talking about the mourning woman but is talking to them. See the notes on 9:17-18 for further explanation.

It is a little difficult to explain how the Hebrew particle כִּי (ki) is functioning here. W. L. Holladay (Jeremiah [Hermeneia], 1:311) may be correct in seeing it as introducing the contents of what those who call for the mourning women are to say. In this case, Jeremiah picks up the task as representative of the people.
Heb “Listen to the word of the Lord.”sn In this context the “word of the Lord” that they are to listen for is the word of the lament that they are to teach their daughters and neighbors.
verses.commentary: 9:20 This verse is addressed to the professional mourners of Jer. 9:17. See note at Jer. 9:17.

verses.zh: 因为死亡上来，进了我们的窗户，入了我们的宫殿；要从外边剪除孩童，从街上剪除少年人。
verses.en: ‘Death has climbed in[NOTE:1] through our windows.It has entered into our fortified houses.It has taken away our children who play in the streets.It has taken away our young men who gather in the city squares.’
notes: Here Death is personified (treated as though it were a person). Some have seen as possible background to this lament an allusion to Mesopotamian mythology where the demon Lamastu climbs in through the windows of houses and over their walls to kill children and babies.
verses.commentary:
9:21 "For death has come up through our windows" This personification of death (cf. personification
of Sheol and death in Hab. 2:5; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELS AND DEMONS)
as coming through the windows is very similar to

- the Canaanite myth of Ba'al being killed by the god of the underworld, Mot, in the Ugaritic
literature found at Ras-Shamra

- the Mesopotamian myth of a female demon (Lamashtu) who climbs through the windows to kill babies

This may be an allusion by the prophet to the type of mythology (Canaanite fertility worship, Molech) to which
the people of God were listening and sacrificing.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP

▣ "To cut off the children. . .The young men" The last two lines of Jer. 9:21 are a way of
saying

- that death is no respecter of persons

- that death will cut off the next generation

verses.zh: 你当说，耶和华如此说：人的尸首必倒在田野像粪土，又像收割的人遗落的一把禾稼，无人收取。
verses.en: Tell your daughters and neighbors, ‘The Lord says:“The dead bodies of people will lie scattered everywherelike manure scattered on a field.They will lie scattered on the ground like grain that has been cut down but has not been gathered.”’”[NOTE:1]
notes: Or vv. 21-22 may read, “‘Death has climbed…city squares. And the dead bodies of people lie scattered…They lie scattered…but has not been gathered.’ The Lord has told me to tell you this.” Or, “For death will climb…It will enter…It will take away…who gather in the city squares. So tell your daughters and neighbors, ‘The Lord wants you to say, “The dead bodies of people lie scattered…They lie scattered…has not been gathered.”’” The main causes of ambiguity are the particle כִּי (ki) introducing v. 21 and the verb form דַּבֵּר (dabber) at the beginning of v. 22. כִּי may be interpreted as introducing a causal sentence giving Jeremiah’s grounds for the commands of v. 19, in which case the verbs would best be understood as prophetic perfects (as in the second alternate translation). Or it may be interpreted as introducing the content of the lament the women are to teach their daughters and neighbors (as in the translation adopted and in the first alternate translation). The form דַּבֵּר may be interpreted as a Piel masculine singular imperative addressed to Jeremiah (as in the first alternate translation, where it is placed at the end for the sake of clarity) or as a Piel infinitive absolute either explaining what the woman are to teach their daughters and neighbors (as in the second alternate translation; cf. GKC 341 §113.h, i for this use of the infinitive absolute) or as equivalent to an imperative addressed to the women, telling them to tell their daughters and neighbors the reason for the lament, i.e., the Lord’s promise of widespread death (cf. GKC 346 §113.bb for this use of the infinitive absolute). The translation chosen has opted for v. 21 as the content of the lament and v. 22 as the further explanation that Jeremiah has the women pass on to their neighbors and daughters. This appears to this interpreter to create the least confusion and dislocation in the flow of the passage.
verses.commentary:
9:22 "The corpses of men will fall like dung on the open field" This is common imagery for the results
of invasion in Jeremiah (cf. Jer. 7:33; 8:2; 16:4; 26:23). It was one of the curses for covenant disobedience in
Deut. 28:26.

▣ "And like the sheaf after the reaper" This is possibly the origin of the modern personification
of death as "the grim reaper," but please note that God, not the evil one, is in control of death (i.e. the
death angel of Exodus 12).

SPECIAL TOPIC: DEATH ANGEL

verses.zh: 耶和华如此说：「智慧人不要因他的智慧夸口，勇士不要因他的勇力夸口，财主不要因他的财物夸口。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] The Lord says,“Wise people should not boast that they are wise.Powerful people should not boast that they are powerful.[NOTE:2] Rich people should not boast that they are rich.[NOTE:3]
notes: It is not always clear why verses were placed in their present position in the editorial process of collecting Jeremiah’s sermons and the words the Lord spoke to him (see Jer 36:4, 32 for reference to two of these collections). Here it is probable that vv. 23-26 were added as a further answer to the question raised in v. 12.
Or “Strong people should not brag that they are strong.”
Heb “…in their wisdom…in their power…in their riches.”
verses.commentary:
9:23-24 This is a beautiful description of true wisdom in contrast with the false wisdom of the
scribes mentioned earlier in Jer. 8:8-12. Note the fivefold repetition of "glory" (BDB 237, KB 248).

- four Hithpael IMPERFECTS used in a JUSSIVE sense

- one Hithpael PARTICIPLE in Jer. 9:24

9:23 "Let not a wise man boast of his wisdom" The wise person will know that it is not in human
might or riches but in YHWH that one's strength lies (cf. Zech. 4:6).

verses.zh: 夸口的却因他有聪明，认识我是耶和华，又知道我喜悦在世上施行慈爱、公平，和公义，以此夸口。这是耶和华说的。」
verses.en: If people want to boast, they should boast about this:They should boast that they understand and know me.They should boast that they know and understandthat I, the Lord, act out of faithfulness, fairness, and justice in the earthand that I desire people to do these things,”[NOTE:1] says the Lord.
notes: Or “fairness and justice, because these things give me pleasure.” Verse 24 reads in Hebrew, “But let the one who brags brag in this: understanding and knowing me, that I, the Lord, do faithfulness, justice, and righteousness in the earth, for/that I delight in these.” It is uncertain whether the Hebrew particle כִּי (ki) before the clause “I delight in these things” is parallel to the כִּי introducing the clause “that I, the Lord, act…,” or whether it is causal, giving the grounds for the Lord acting the way he does. In light of the contrasts in the passage and the emphasis that Jeremiah has placed on obedience to the covenant and ethical conduct in conjunction with real allegiance to the Lord, not mere lip service, it is probable that the clauses are parallel. For the use of כִּי to introduce clauses of further definition after a direct object, as here, see GKC 365 §117.h and see BDB 393 s.v. יָדַע Qal.1.a. For parallels to the idea of Yahweh requiring these characteristics in people, see Hos 6:6, Mic 6:8.
verses.commentary:
9:24 "but let him who boasts boast of this, that he understands and knows Me, that I am
the Lord"

Notice all the things that humans tend to boast in

- wisdom

- strength

- wealth

are not what should be gloried in, but

- that he/she understands Me ‒ BDB 968, KB 1328, Hiphil INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE

- that he/she knows Me ‒ BDB 393, KB 390, Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE

These INFINITIVES speak of human reception of divine revelation. They have
heard and responded to the law of YHWH, the voice of YHWH (cf. Jer. 9:13) and the Person of YHWH
(i.e. "Me," Jer. 9:24; Hosea 4:1,6; 5:4; 8:2)! This is the opposite of Jer. 9:3d and 6.

Characteristics of YHWH are delineated in this verse. The mandate that believers boast
in God is a common biblical theme (cf. Jer. 4:2; Ps. 44:8; Isa. 41:16; 1 Cor. 1:31; 2 Cor. 10:17;
Gal. 6:14).

The characteristics of God in Jer. 9:24 can also be seen beautifully expressed in
Exod. 34:6,7 and Neh. 9:17.

- lovingkindness (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS [hesed])

- justice (see SPECIAL TOPIC: JUSTICE)

- righteousness (see SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS)

▣ "for I delight in these things" If YHWH "delights" (BDB 342, KB 339, Qal
PERFECT) in the above mentioned things, then we should take special notice of them and
emulate them (cf. Isa. 58:2; opposite of Jer. 11:10; 13:10; also note Micah 6:8).

verses.zh: 耶和华说：「看哪，日子将到，我要刑罚一切受过割礼、心却未受割礼的，
verses.en: The Lord says, “Watch out![NOTE:1] The time is soon coming when I will punish all those who are circumcised only in the flesh.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Behold!”
Heb “punish all who are circumcised in the flesh.” The translation is contextually motivated to better bring out the contrast that follows.
verses.commentary:
9:25-26 This is a theological contrast between physical circumcision and spiritual circumcision.
Circumcision was an outward sign of the covenant between YHWH and Abraham (cf. Gen. 17:10). All of the
surrounding nations practiced circumcision, but not for the same spiritual purposes as Israel. The only
uncircumcised people in the Ancient Near East that we know of were the Philistines, a group of mercenaries
from Aegean Islands who invaded Palestine around the middle of the twelfth century B.C. But,
although circumcision was meant to be a sign of the covenant, what God really wanted was an inner attitude
of love for Him, as well as the outward covenant stipulations. This is why the Bible repeatedly speaks of
different parts of the body being circumcised:

- the ears, Jer. 6:10

- the lips, Exod. 6:12,30

- the heart, Lev. 26:41; Deut. 10:16; 30:6; Jer. 4:4; Ezek. 44:7,9

This same radical truth is reflected in the NT in Rom. 2:28,29! As temple ritual and liturgy
without faith offered no hope, so too, family liturgy and ritual without faith offered no hope
(i.e. Jeremiah 7)!

verses.zh: 就是埃及、犹大、以东、亚扪人、摩押人，和一切住在旷野剃周围头发的；因为列国人都没有受割礼，以色列人心中也没有受割礼。」
verses.en: That is, I will punish the Egyptians, the Judeans, the Edomites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, and all the desert people who cut their hair short at the temples.[NOTE:1] I will do so because none of the people of those nations are really circumcised in the Lord’s sight.[NOTE:2] Moreover, none of the people of Israel[NOTE:3] are circumcised when it comes to their hearts.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “all those who are cut off on the side of the head who live in the desert.” KJV and some other English versions (e.g., NIV11 “who live in the wilderness in distant places”; NLT “who live in distant places”) have followed the interpretation that this is a biform of an expression meaning, “end or remote parts of the [far] corners [of the earth].” This interpretation is generally abandoned by the more recent commentaries and lexicons (see, e.g. BDB 802 s.v. פֵּאָה 1 and HALOT 858 s.v. פֵּאָה 1.β). It occurs also in 25:33; 49:32.

Heb “For all of these nations are uncircumcised.” The words “I will do so” are supplied in the translation to indicate the connection with the preceding statement.sn Circumcision as a mere external cutting of the flesh is contrasted here with it as a sign of commitment to the covenant and the God of the covenant. The people of these nations practiced circumcision, but not as a sign of the covenant. The people of Israel engaged in it as a religious practice, but without any obedience to the covenant that it was a sign of, or any real commitment to the Lord.
Heb “house of Israel.”
Heb “And all the house of Israel is uncircumcised of heart.”
verses.commentary:
9:26 "who clip the hair on their temples" There have been four basic interpretations of this Hebrew
phrase.

- The NASB, REV, and NJB interpret this as an idolatrous act reflected in Lev. 19:27; Jer. 25:23; 49:32.

- It may relate to mourning for the dead (cf. Deut. 14:1).

- It may be to a part of the idolatrous worship of the foreign gods (cf. Herodotus 111,8).

- The other interpretation is found in the NKJV, NIV, and REB, which translate this as imagery for the
universal judgment of God (i.e. NKJV, "and all who are in the farthest corners, who dwell in the wilderness").

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

And my eyes a fountain of tears,

A wayfarers' lodging place;

And go from them!

For all of them are adulterers,

An assembly of treacherous men.

3"They bend their tongue like their bow;

4"Let everyone be on guard against his neighbor,

And do not trust any brother;

Because every brother deals craftily,

And every neighbor goes about as a slanderer.

5Everyone deceives his neighbor

And does not speak the truth,

They have taught their tongue to speak lies;

6Your dwelling is in the midst of deceit;

Through deceit they refuse to know Me," declares the Lord
